items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: Uh, played a few jobs with Nicholas and, uh, with Danny.

ctx.x: What about the other New Orleans musicians up there?

Well, you mean, aside from Bunk's band? Yeah. Well, I, uh, got to know Danny Barker and Alan Nicholas, uh, while I was up there more than any other, uh, of the New Orleans musicians. Uh, played a few jobs with Nicholas and, uh, with Danny. Mm-hmm. And, uh, Pops Foster.
What do you think of their approach as compared with the approach of, say, the Joyce Lewis group, or with Lone Johnson's approach?

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: the loudest instrument in the band was Danny Barker's guitar, an unamplified guitar, and you could hear it ringing through the whole hall.

ctx.x: Did Bunk ever mention to you about the dynamics of playing the starting out the first chorus loud or the hitting the introduction hard as they sometimes say here?

No, but I'll tell you something I wanted to remember about this band, that they achieved this terrific thing of playing so quietly that you could just barely hear the band. The loudest instrument in the band, and this wasn't at first now, but toward the end of the engagement, the loudest instrument in the band was Danny Barker's guitar, an unamplified guitar, and you could hear it ringing through the whole hall.
The whole bunch was playing that song.
